1.title: Rangen vs Muenchberg: Two Kinds of Volcanic Geology Compared
1.items.0.label: Rangen (Thann & Vieux-Thann)
1.items.0.desc: The southernmost and only true volcanic site in Alsace: siliceous rock and basaltic lava, dark and stony, with excellent heat storage. The Thur river runs at the foot of the hill, protecting against spring frost. 22.13 ha, Riesling / Pinot Gris / Gewurztraminer. Thann is the only town in Alsace where "the entire commune's vineyards are classified Grand Cru".
1.items.1.label: Muenchberg (Nothalten)
1.items.1.desc: The 901 m Ungersberg sandstone hill shields it from rain-bearing westerlies. The geology is Permian (250 million years ago) volcanic-clastic deposits (with volcanic ash and tuff), stony and poor but very well-drained and quick to warm. 17.70 ha, mainly Riesling. Cistercian monks were already farming here in the 12th century.
2.title: Rangen: A Legend on Lava
2.html:
From the 13th century, monks making pilgrimages to the church of Saint-Thiébaut in Thann already praised Rangen; 16th-century writers Fischart and Brand, and even Michel de Montaigne in his 1580 travel journal, described the site as the "most beautiful and best-cultivated" vineyard scene.

In style: Riesling shows elegant, delicate fruit, while Pinot Gris and Gewurztraminer excel in power and varietal character — Alsace's most distinctive "volcanic" flavour.
3.question: What is the unique feature of the Rangen site?
3.options.0: It is the largest Grand Cru in Alsace
3.options.1: It is the only true volcanic site in Alsace, and Thann is the only town whose entire commune is classified Grand Cru
3.options.2: It is the only Grand Cru allowed to plant Chardonnay
3.options.3: It is the highest-altitude Grand Cru
3.explanation: Rangen is the only Grand Cru in Alsace made of true volcanic rock (siliceous rock and basaltic lava), and also the southernmost Grand Cru of the region. In addition, Thann is Alsace's special case where "the vineyards of the entire town commune are classified Grand Cru".
4.keyPoints.0: Rangen (Thann, 22.13 ha): the only true volcanic site in Alsace, southernmost Grand Cru, with the whole Thann commune classified Grand Cru
4.keyPoints.1: Muenchberg (Nothalten, 17.70 ha): Permian volcanic-clastic rock, rain shielded by the Ungersberg, known for Riesling
4.keyPoints.2: What dark volcanic rocks share: good heat storage and drainage, creating a concentrated and distinctive flavour signature
